spec.expr: max by (pod) (time() - process_start_time_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) < 60

description: grafana-infinity-datasource-cache: clients, keys, refreshes, upstreams, Redis, runtime and logs. https://github.com/sakharovmaksim/grafana-infinity-datasource-cache

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, source) (rate(datasource_cache_served_age_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_ttl_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})
max(datasource_cache_config_max_stale_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description:
p99 age of data at the moment it is served — what dashboards actually show. Dashed — the source TTL, red dashed — max_stale.

The histogram is coarse (buckets 1m…7d), the value is stepped. Normally below TTL: keys are refreshed ahead.

Above TTL clients get STALE; at the max_stale line the next answer is 502.

**What to do:**
1. Which key is old — "Per-key state".
2. Why it is not refreshed — Refreshes and Upstreams tabs.
spec.title: Served data age

spec.expr: sum by (source, encoding) (rate(datasource_cache_response_bytes_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Response body bytes sent to clients; identity — decompressed on the fly for a client without gzip.

Infinity sends Accept-Encoding: gzip, so identity costs CPU and is normally small.

**What to do:**
1. identity grows together with CPU — find the client without gzip (not Grafana).
spec.title: Response throughput

spec.expr: sum by (source, code) (rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source", code!~"2.."}[$__rate_interval])) / ignoring (code) group_left sum by (source) (rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Share of responses by code: 5xx — proxy failures, 499 — canceled by the client, 4xx — client errors passed through.

Empty until non-2xx series appear; NaN without traffic.

**What to do:**
1. 502/504 — Upstreams tab and "Keys without data".
2. 4xx — wrong query in the client dashboard.
spec.title: Non-2xx share by source and code

spec.expr: sum by (le) (increase(datasource_cache_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Latency distribution of all responses.

Normal: a dense band in milliseconds (hit) and rare dots in seconds (miss). A second band in seconds means clients keep waiting for upstreams.

**What to do:**
1. Split by result — "Latency by result".

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Latency distribution

spec.expr: sum by (pod, source) (datasource_cache_requests_in_flight{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Client requests being processed, by replica and source.

A gauge at scrape time: short hit bursts are invisible. A steady non-zero level means clients hang on cold keys or slow response writes.

**What to do:**
1. Compare with miss in "Requests by cache result" and "Lock waits".
2. One replica holds much more than the others — check Service balancing and that replica's CPU.
spec.title: Requests in flight

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, result) (rate(datasource_cache_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, result) (rate(datasource_cache_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_miss_wait_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Response latency by cache result, including writing the body; p99 solid, p50 dashed, the sources' miss_wait — red dashed.

hit/stale take milliseconds (replica memory, gzip). miss and error include the upstream wait and stop at miss_wait. Slower hit without more traffic — CPU throttling, GC or reading an evicted copy from Redis.

miss at the miss_wait line — cold requests get 504.

**What to do:**
1. Slow hit — Runtime tab (throttling, scheduler latency) and "Lookups by result" (loaded).
2. Slow miss — "Upstream attempt duration" and "Upstream waits".
spec.title: Latency by result

spec.expr: sum by (reason) (increase(datasource_cache_rejected_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (source) (increase(datasource_cache_coalesced_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Requests rejected before the cache, by reason, and cold requests that joined a fetch already running in the same replica.

coalesced is the normal protection of an upstream from a crowd: N clients on a new key make one fetch. rejected means client misconfiguration or path bypass attempts.

**What to do:**
1. unsafe_path — treat as a security incident.
2. unknown_source / not_allowed — compare the datasource URL and method with the source config.
3. body_too_large — the POST body is above the limit.

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Rejected / coalesced

spec.expr: sum by (result) (rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Client requests by cache result.

hit — a fresh copy, stale — an old copy (a background refresh runs), miss — no key, the client waits for the upstream, bypass — above max_keys, error — 5xx, canceled — the client left before the answer (499). Normally almost everything is hit.

**What to do:**
1. More stale — the upstream is slow or failing: Upstreams tab.
2. More miss — new keys or evictions: "Keys by state", "Lookups by result".
3. More bypass — the "Bypass, 15m" tile.
spec.title: Requests by cache result

spec.expr: max by (source) (datasource_cache_entry_max_age_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}) / on (source) max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_ttl_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

scalar(max(datasource_cache_config_max_stale_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})) / max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_ttl_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Age of the oldest key / TTL: ≥1 — freshness lost, ≥2 — not refreshed for a long time (the README alert). An early signal, not the hard limit; the red dashed line is max_stale, after which clients get 502.

A key without data is reported with the max_stale age — check "Keys without data".

**What to do:**
1. Which key — "Per-key state".
2. Why — Refreshes and Upstreams tabs.
spec.title: Oldest data / TTL

spec.expr: sum by (source) (max by (source, state) (datasource_cache_entries{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})) / (max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_max_keys{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}) > 0)

spec.description: Approximate tracked keys / max_keys: tracked keys include warmup, while the limit excludes it, so this is not exact utilization. Confirm the limit by BYPASS. max_keys = 0 means unlimited, no line is drawn.
spec.title: Tracked keys / max_keys (estimate)

spec.expr: max by (source, state) (datasource_cache_entries{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Tracked keys by state: fresh — younger than TTL, stale — older than TTL but younger than max_stale, missing — no data.

Computed from the shared store every refresh_interval, the same on all replicas. Keys not requested for idle_ttl are deleted with their data.

Any missing key means clients get 502/504; the stale share grows when an upstream is not refreshed.

**What to do:**
1. The keys — "Per-key state", the cause — logs (`fetch failed`).
2. A sharp growth of keys — `${__from}` in a URL: see "Tracked keys / max_keys".
spec.title: Keys by state

spec.expr: max by (source, encoding) (datasource_cache_stored_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Size of the tracked entries: gzip — space taken in Redis, identity — uncompressed size.

If Redis is shared with other applications under allkeys-lru, growth evicts their data and ours.

**What to do:**
1. Who grows — "Per-key state" (size).
2. A sharp growth — a new heavy query or `${__from}` in a URL.
spec.title: Stored bytes

spec.expr: max by (source, request) (datasource_cache_entry_age_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

max by (source, request) (datasource_cache_entry_age_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}) / on (source) group_left max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_ttl_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})
max by (source, request) (datasource_cache_entry_size_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})
time() - max by (source, request) (datasource_cache_entry_last_access_timestamp_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})
max by (source, request) (datasource_cache_entry_failing{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
State of every key (up to METRICS_ENTRY_LIMIT): age, age in TTLs, uncompressed size, time since the last client request, result of the last refresh.

A key without age has no data (missing). idle close to idle_ttl — the key will soon be deleted with its data. request is the path and query as in the datasource URL.

age / TTL: yellow — STALE, red — the upstream does not refresh the key.

**What to do:**
1. FAILED — the error in the logs by request (`fetch failed`), its class — "Upstream errors by reason".
2. Many similar keys — time macros in the URL of the client dashboard.
spec.title: Per-key state

spec.expr: sum by (level) (count_over_time({cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} | json level="level" [$__interval]))

spec.description:
Service log lines by level.

At the info level the per-request debug messages (`served`, `client gave up`) are not logged; the request flow is in the metrics. INFO — start, config, `fetched` for every fetch.

**What to do:**
1. A WARN/ERROR spike — "WARN / ERROR by message" and "Top warnings".
spec.title: Log lines by level

spec.expr: {cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} |= "$search" | json lvl="level" | lvl=~"$level"

spec.description:
Service logs: the JSON line of slog (msg, request, error, trigger, size, duration in nanoseconds).

Filters — the "Log level" and "Search" variables (a substring of the raw line).

**What to do:**
1. Find the error of a key by its path from "Per-key state" in "Search".
spec.title: Logs

spec.expr: topk(20, max by (req, trigger) (max_over_time({cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} | json msg="msg", req="request", trigger="trigger", dur="duration" | msg="fetched" | unwrap dur | __error__="" [$__range]))) / 1000000000

spec.description:
The slowest successful key fetches in the range (from `fetched` lines): time under the lock with retries, limits and the Redis write.

Metrics give durations per source only, this is per request. Keys close to the source timeout are candidates for 504 on a cold request.

**What to do:**
1. Compare with "Upstream attempt duration" and the source timeout; a heavy key — narrow the query in the client dashboard.
spec.title: Slowest fetches

spec.expr: topk(50, sum by (lvl, msg, err) (count_over_time({cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} | json lvl="level", msg="msg", err="error" | lvl=~"WARN|ERROR" [$__range])))

spec.description:
The most frequent WARN/ERROR lines in the range, with the error text.

The error text contains the request and the cause (timeout, upstream code), so one upstream failure gives a line per key.

**What to do:**
1. Match the error class with "Upstream errors by reason"; the time — "Logs".
spec.title: Top warnings

spec.expr: sum by (msg) (count_over_time({cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} | json level="level", msg="msg" | level=~"WARN|ERROR" [$__interval]))

spec.description:
WARN and ERROR by message.

fetch failed — a key fetch failed; fetch lock lost — the lease expired; store unavailable — Redis failure; source is at max_keys — BYPASS; request failed — 5xx to a client; corrupt cache entry — a broken entry.

**What to do:**
1. Details — "Top warnings" and "Logs" filtered by level.
spec.title: WARN / ERROR by message

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, result) (rate(datasource_cache_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, result) (rate(datasource_cache_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_miss_wait_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Response latency by cache result, including writing the body; p99 solid, p50 dashed, the sources' miss_wait — red dashed.

hit/stale take milliseconds (replica memory, gzip). miss and error include the upstream wait and stop at miss_wait. Slower hit without more traffic — CPU throttling, GC or reading an evicted copy from Redis.

miss at the miss_wait line — cold requests get 504.

**What to do:**
1. Slow hit — Runtime tab (throttling, scheduler latency) and "Lookups by result" (loaded).
2. Slow miss — "Upstream attempt duration" and "Upstream waits".
spec.title: Latency by result

spec.expr: sum by (result) (rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Client requests by cache result.

hit — a fresh copy, stale — an old copy (a background refresh runs), miss — no key, the client waits for the upstream, bypass — above max_keys, error — 5xx, canceled — the client left before the answer (499). Normally almost everything is hit.

**What to do:**
1. More stale — the upstream is slow or failing: Upstreams tab.
2. More miss — new keys or evictions: "Keys by state", "Lookups by result".
3. More bypass — the "Bypass, 15m" tile.
spec.title: Requests by cache result

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(go_gc_heap_allocs_bytes_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (pod) (increase(go_gc_cycles_total_gc_cycles_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Heap allocation rate and GC cycles (right axis), per pod.

Allocation spikes match fetches of large bodies and decompression for clients without gzip.

**What to do:**
1. More allocation without more traffic — compare with "Response throughput" (identity) and "Downloaded from upstream".

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Heap allocation rate / GC cycles

spec.expr: sum by (pod, cause) (rate(promhttp_metric_handler_errors_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description: The metrics handler uses ContinueOnError: HTTP 200 does not guarantee a complete scrape. Collector errors explain missing series.
spec.title: Metrics collector errors

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!="", container!="POD", metrics_path=~"/metrics/cadvisor|"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (pod) sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="cpu", container!=""})

spec.description: CPU usage / limit: ≥80% — warning, ≥95% — saturation risk. Without a CPU limit there is no series. Judge by ≥5 minutes and latency growth; throttling is on "CPU throttled periods".
spec.title: CPU usage / limit

spec.expr: max by (pod) (process_open_fds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) / (max by (pod) (process_max_fds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) > 0)

spec.description: Open FDs / process_max_fds: ≥70% — check the growth of open connections and files, ≥90% — little headroom before EMFILE.
spec.title: File descriptor utilization

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, pod) (rate(go_gc_pauses_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, pod) (rate(go_sched_latencies_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.description: p99 GC pause and scheduler latency: ≥10 ms — check GC/CPU pressure, ≥50 ms — a noticeable delay for the fast cache path. Engineering guides, not a latency SLO; with few events p99 is noisy.
spec.title: GC pause / sched latency p99

spec.expr: max by (pod) (go_goroutines{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})
max by (pod) (go_threads{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})
max by (pod) (process_open_fds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description:
Goroutines, OS threads and open file descriptors, per pod.

Goroutines follow requests in flight and fetches. Monotonic growth without load growth is a leak (stuck fetches, unclosed connections).

**What to do:**
1. Goroutines grow together with "Slot saturation" — hanging upstream fetches.
2. Take a goroutine dump before restarting.
spec.title: Goroutines / threads / FDs

spec.expr: max by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!="", container!="POD", metrics_path=~"/metrics/cadvisor|"}) / on (pod) sum by (pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", resource="memory", container!=""})

max by (pod) (go_memory_classes_total_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"} - go_memory_classes_heap_released_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) / max by (pod) (go_gc_gomemlimit_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description: Working set / container memory limit: ≥80% — little headroom, ≥90% — high risk of running out, especially while fetching large bodies. Go memory / GOMEMLIMIT (dashed) is the GC soft target, without alert thresholds; read it together with GC pauses and CPU.
spec.title: Memory vs limit

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (pod) (rate(process_network_receive_bytes_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (pod) (rate(process_network_transmit_bytes_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Container restarts (bars) and process network traffic rx/tx (right axis), per pod.

rx is mostly upstreams and Redis, tx — responses to clients and Redis.

**What to do:**
1. A restart — the cause in `kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason`, OOM — "Memory vs limit".

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Restarts / network

spec.expr: min by (pod) (up{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description: up = 0 — the scrape failed (red), up = 1 — OK (green). A vanished target is a gap / No data, not green. HTTP 200 may still carry an incomplete set of metrics — see "Metrics collector errors".
spec.title: Scrape health

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!="", container!="POD", metrics_path=~"/metrics/cadvisor|"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", container!="", container!="POD", metrics_path=~"/metrics/cadvisor|"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description: Share of CFS periods with throttling: ≥10% — warning, ≥25% — critical. This is not the share of lost CPU; judge by ≥5 minutes and client latency.
spec.title: CPU throttled periods

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, source, trigger) (rate(datasource_cache_refresh_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_miss_wait_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Fetch duration under the lock: retries, waits for the rate limiter and slots, the Redis write. Red dashed — miss_wait.

For miss this is what the client waits: above miss_wait it gets 504, while the fetch goes on and fills the cache.

**What to do:**
1. Split it: "Upstream attempt duration" (the upstream itself), "Upstream waits" (limits), "Store op latency p99" (Redis).
spec.title: Refresh duration

spec.expr: sum by (outcome) (increase(datasource_cache_lock_waits_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (source) (increase(datasource_cache_lock_lost_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Cold requests that waited for a fetch of another replica, by outcome, and lost lock leases.

entry — got the data; failure — the other replica's fetch failed; released — the lock was released without data; timeout — gave up waiting. lock lost — the lease (30 s with heartbeat) expired before the fetch ended: the key may have been fetched twice.

**What to do:**
1. timeout — "Lock wait p99" against miss_wait, a slow upstream.
2. lock lost — heartbeats do not reach Redis: "Store op latency p99", "Store errors", CPU throttling.

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Lock waits / lock lost

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, source) (rate(datasource_cache_lock_wait_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_miss_wait_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
p99 wait of a cold request for a fetch run by another replica. Red dashed — miss_wait.

Close to the "Refresh duration" of other replicas; at the miss_wait line waiting clients get 504.

**What to do:**
1. Compare with "Upstream attempt duration": a slow upstream or a stuck lease.
spec.title: Lock wait p99

spec.expr: (time() - max by (pod, source) (datasource_cache_refresh_cycle_last_timestamp_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})) / on (pod) group_left() (max by (pod) (datasource_cache_config_refresh_interval_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) > 0)

spec.description:
Time since the last background refresh pass / refresh_interval, per replica and source: ≥2 — expected passes were missed, ≥5 — the loop or its slots are stuck (README alert).

**What to do:**
1. "Slot saturation" and "Upstream waits" (Upstreams).
spec.title: Refresh loop lag

spec.expr: sum by (trigger, result) (increase(datasource_cache_refreshes_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Refresh attempts by trigger (miss — a cold request, stale — an old copy was served, scheduled — refresh-ahead) and result.

success — fetched; locked — another replica is fetching; current — another replica has just refreshed it, the upstream was not called; backoff — skipped after a recent failure; error — failed. Normally scheduled/success and scheduled/locked|current.

**What to do:**
1. error/backoff — "Upstream errors by reason" and `fetch failed` in the logs.
2. Many stale/* — the background cannot keep up: "Refresh loop lag", "Slot saturation".

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Refreshes by trigger / result

spec.expr: sum by (op) (increase(datasource_cache_store_errors_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (pod) (increase(datasource_cache_redis_pool_timeouts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Failed Redis operations by type and pool connection wait timeouts.

On a failure the replica serves from memory; a 5 s breaker cuts repeated calls. A pool timeout means all connections are held by slow operations.

**What to do:**
1. `store unavailable` in the logs — the error text.
2. Pool timeouts without Redis errors — "Store op latency p99" and "Redis pool".

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Store errors / pool timeouts

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, op) (rate(datasource_cache_store_operation_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.description:
p99 of Redis operations: ≥50 ms — degraded, ≥250 ms — a noticeable delay on the cache path. The store timeout in code is 3 s.

**What to do:**
1. Check errors, pool waits and client latency together.
spec.title: Store op latency p99

spec.expr: max by (pod) (datasource_cache_local_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) / on (pod) (max by (pod) (datasource_cache_config_local_max_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) > 0)
max by (pod) (datasource_cache_local_entries{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description: Gzipped local copies / local_max_bytes: ≥90% — the cache is close to its limit, a capacity warning, not an outage. A full cache is normal by itself; evictions are confirmed by local_evictions and their impact by loaded lookups and latency. On the right — the number of copies.
spec.title: Replica memory copies

spec.expr: sum by (result) (rate(datasource_cache_lookups_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum(increase(datasource_cache_local_evictions_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Where a request found its data: local — replica memory, loaded — no copy, read from Redis synchronously, absent — nowhere, error — no copy and Redis is unavailable. Bars on the right — copies evicted by local_max_bytes.

Normally almost everything is local. loaded grows after restarts and evictions — a synchronous Redis read on the client path.

**What to do:**
1. loaded with constant evictions — local_max_bytes is too small for the key set: "Replica memory copies".
2. error — Redis is unavailable: the "Redis" tile.

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Lookups by result

spec.expr: max by (pod, state) (datasource_cache_redis_pool_connections{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})
sum by (pod) (increase(datasource_cache_redis_pool_waits_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Pool connections per replica (total, idle); on the right — how often a request waited for a free connection.

idle close to total — the pool is idle. Waits without more traffic — slow operations hold connections.

**What to do:**
1. "Store op latency p99", "Store errors / pool timeouts".

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Redis pool

spec.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(datasource_cache_redis_pool_wait_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (pod) (rate(datasource_cache_redis_pool_waits_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

spec.description: Mean wait for a pool connection among the waits. No line without waits; read together with timeouts and the connection count.
spec.title: Redis pool mean wait

spec.expr: sum by (result) (increase(datasource_cache_revalidations_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Background reconciliation of the replica copy with Redis every local_check: current — the same, updated — new metadata, loaded — Redis has a newer body (another replica refreshed it), kept — Redis has no copy or an older one, error — Redis is unavailable.

A constant kept means Redis loses entries (allkeys-lru evictions or a recreated Redis).

**What to do:**
1. kept — Redis maxmemory and evicted_keys.
2. error — the "Redis" tile.

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Revalidations by result

spec.expr: max by (pod) (datasource_cache_store_up{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description:
Redis answer to the ping in the refresh pass, per replica.

DOWN on one replica — its network or pool; on all — Redis itself. The replica keeps serving from memory. No data without Redis configured.

**What to do:**
1. "Store errors / pool timeouts", "Store op latency p99".
2. Check the Redis instance: pod, maxmemory, limits.
spec.title: Redis reachable

spec.expr: (sum(rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source", code=~"5.."}[5m])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[5m]))

spec.description:
5xx responses / all responses over 5 minutes: ≥0.1% — warning, ≥1% — high failure rate. Visual guides, not an SLO.

With a few requests a single failure moves the share a lot: check the absolute count and code. No traffic is grey, not green.

**What to do:**
1. Which source and code — "Non-2xx share by source and code" (Clients).
2. 502/504 — Upstreams tab; keys without data — "Keys without data".
spec.title: 5xx share, 5m

spec.expr: max by (source) (datasource_cache_entry_max_age_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}) / on (source) max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_ttl_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Age of the oldest key / TTL: ≥1 — freshness lost, ≥2 — not refreshed for a long time (the README alert). An early signal, not the hard limit: data is served until max_stale.

A key without data is reported with the max_stale age — check "Keys without data".

**What to do:**
1. Which key — "Per-key state" (Keys).
2. Why — Refreshes and Upstreams tabs.
spec.title: Oldest data / TTL

spec.expr: sum(increase(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source", result="bypass"}[15m])) or (0 * sum(datasource_cache_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}))

spec.description:
Requests that bypassed the cache over 15 minutes: the source already holds max_keys keys, so a new key is fetched without storing.

The usual cause is `${__from}`/`${__to}` in an Infinity query URL: every dashboard refresh is a new key.

Yellow — the source is at its limit (the README alert).

**What to do:**
1. "Per-key state": many keys with the same path and different time parameters.
2. `source is at max_keys` in the logs.
3. Remove time macros from the dashboard query, or raise max_keys if the keys are legitimate.
spec.title: Bypass, 15m

spec.expr: sum(max by (source) (datasource_cache_entries_failing{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}))

spec.description:
Keys whose last refresh failed; while the copy is younger than max_stale, clients get STALE.

A key with data that gets 4xx stays here — that is what an expired API key looks like.

Yellow — the upstream answers with errors, data is ageing.

**What to do:**
1. The cause — "Upstream errors by reason"; http_4xx on all keys of a source — check its API key and quota.
2. Time left before 502 — "Oldest data / TTL" against the max_stale line.
spec.title: Failing keys

spec.expr: sum(rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source", result=~"hit|stale"}[1h])) / sum(rate(datasource_cache_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[1h]))

spec.description:
Share of HIT + STALE responses over an hour, informational, without a red/green status.

New keys and cold starts lower it naturally, and a high share does not prove freshness: STALE counts too. Check 5xx, latency and served age.
spec.title: Served from cache, 1h

spec.expr: max((time() - max by (pod, source) (datasource_cache_refresh_cycle_last_timestamp_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})) / on (pod) group_left() (max by (pod) (datasource_cache_config_refresh_interval_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}) > 0))

spec.description:
Time since the last background refresh pass / refresh_interval: ≥2 — expected passes were missed, ≥5 — the loop or its slots are stuck (README alert). Worst replica and source.

**What to do:**
1. "Slot saturation" and "Upstream waits" (Upstreams).
spec.title: Refresh loop lag

spec.expr: sum(max by (source) (datasource_cache_entries{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source", state="missing"}))

spec.description:
Tracked keys without usable data: clients get 502/504 for them.

A key that never had data and gets 4xx from the upstream stops being tracked, so this counts only upstream failures or copies older than max_stale.

Red — any such key (the README alert).

**What to do:**
1. Which key — "Per-key state" (failing = 1, empty age).
2. The error — "Top warnings" (Logs).
3. The upstream is down — contact its owner.
spec.title: Keys without data

spec.expr: max(kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"$deployment"}) / (max(kube_deployment_spec_replicas{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~"$deployment"}) > 0)

spec.description:
Ready / desired replicas of the Deployment: 0 — no ready replica, between 0 and 1 — partially ready, 1 — all desired replicas are ready. The Pod filter does not apply.

No data (desired = 0 or no kube-state-metrics) is grey, not green.

**What to do:**
1. Not ready — `kubectl rollout status` and pod events; a config error stops a new replica at start (Logs tab).
spec.title: Replicas ready

spec.expr: min(datasource_cache_store_up{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description:
Whether Redis answers the ping of every replica (minimum over replicas).

Without Redis replicas serve from their own memory: each fetches from upstreams itself, there are no shared locks or backoff, new replicas start empty.

Red — at least one replica cannot reach Redis. No data is expected without Redis configured.

**What to do:**
1. "Store errors / pool timeouts" and "Store op latency p99" (Redis).
2. Check the Redis instance: pod, maxmemory, network.
spec.title: Redis

spec.expr: sum(increase(datasource_cache_rejected_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) or (0 * sum(datasource_cache_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}))

spec.description:
Requests rejected before the cache: unknown source, a path outside `paths` or with `..`, a method that is not allowed, a body that is too large.

unsafe_path is an attempt to leave the allowed paths of a source that the proxy calls with an API key.

Yellow — there are rejections: a wrong datasource URL or a bypass attempt.

**What to do:**
1. The reason — "Rejected / coalesced" (Clients).
2. unknown_source / not_allowed — compare the datasource URL with the config.
3. Unexplained unsafe_path — treat as a security incident.
spec.title: Rejected, 1h

spec.expr: sum(increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[1h])) or (0 * sum(datasource_cache_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}))

spec.description:
Container restarts of the selected pods over a fixed hour: ≥1 — check the cause, ≥3 — repeated failures. A rollout with new pod names is not a restart.

**What to do:**
1. The cause — `kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason`; OOM — "Memory vs limit" (Runtime).
spec.title: Restarts, 1h

spec.expr: count by (version, revision, goversion) (datasource_cache_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

spec.description:
Service and Go version by number of replicas.

Two tiles — a rollout is in progress or stuck halfway.

**What to do:**
1. A stuck rollout — `kubectl rollout status` and pod events; a config error stops a new replica at start and is printed in its log.
spec.title: Version

spec.expr: sum by (source) (rate(datasource_cache_upstream_response_size_bytes_sum{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Uncompressed volume downloaded from upstreams.

A flat background from refresh-ahead; a step up — new heavy keys or frequent retries of large bodies.

**What to do:**
1. Compare with "Upstream attempts by code" and "Stored bytes".
spec.title: Downloaded from upstream

spec.expr: sum by (source, code) (increase(datasource_cache_upstream_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Upstream request attempts by HTTP code; error — no response (network, timeout).

Every attempt, retries included. A flat background is refresh-ahead once per TTL per key; spikes are cold keys and restarts.

**What to do:**
1. Non-2xx and error — the cause in "Upstream errors by reason".
2. More attempts without more keys — frequent retries, or `current` does not work (Redis).

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Upstream attempts by code

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, source) (rate(datasource_cache_upstream_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, source) (rate(datasource_cache_upstream_request_duration_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))
max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_timeout_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
One attempt: from sending the request to reading the whole body. p99 solid, p50 dashed, the source timeout — red dashed.

Large feeds (NVD) may take minutes — that is the upstream. Growth of p50 — the upstream or the network is slower overall; growth of p99 only — individual heavy keys.

p99 at the timeout line — attempts are cut (reason timeout), followed by retries and 504.

**What to do:**
1. Which keys are slow — "Slowest fetches" (Logs).
2. Raise timeout/miss_wait together with the Infinity datasource timeout.
spec.title: Upstream attempt duration

spec.expr: sum by (source, reason) (increase(datasource_cache_upstream_errors_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum by (source) (increase(datasource_cache_upstream_retries_total{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval]))

spec.description:
Failed attempts by reason; dashed — retries.

Network: timeout, eof, reset, refused, dns, tls (eof/reset from Cloudflare-fronted APIs are usually absorbed by retries). Response: http_429 (upstream rate limit), http_5xx, http_3xx (redirect outside the source), invalid_json, too_large. Own: rate_limiter, slots, auth_secret (the key file could not be read). http_4xx is a client query error, not an upstream failure.

**What to do:**
1. Network errors on all sources — egress from the namespace/cluster; on one — that upstream's availability.
2. http_429 — the source rate is above its quota (rate is per replica: divide by the replica count).
3. too_large — the body is above max_body; invalid_json — a maintenance page or `validate` does not fit.
4. auth_secret, or http_4xx on all keys of a source with a key — the API key and its mounted Secret.

Counters: increase over $__rate_interval, windows overlap — do not sum values over time.
spec.title: Upstream errors by reason

spec.expr: (time() - max by (source) (datasource_cache_upstream_last_success_timestamp_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})) / on (source) max by (source) (datasource_cache_source_ttl_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description: Time since the last successful upstream fetch / TTL, without thresholds: without active keys no fetches are needed, and no success in the selected pod does not mean none in others. For degradation use the age of active keys, missing/failing, errors and loop lag. No series before the first success.
spec.title: Time since last upstream success / TTL

spec.expr: max by (source) (datasource_cache_refreshes_in_flight{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"} / datasource_cache_source_concurrency{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

max by (source) (datasource_cache_upstream_requests_in_flight{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"} / datasource_cache_source_max_in_flight{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"})

spec.description:
Share of busy slots of the worst replica per source: refreshes / concurrency and upstream requests / max_in_flight. ≥75% — few slots left, 100% — all busy.

A short 100% is fine; act when it stays ≥5 minutes together with slot waits, loop lag or 503.
spec.title: Slot saturation

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, source) (rate(datasource_cache_upstream_rate_limit_wait_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, source) (rate(datasource_cache_upstream_slot_wait_seconds_bucket{cluster=~"$cluster", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", source=~"$source"}[$__rate_interval])))

spec.description:
p99 wait of an attempt for the source's own rate limiter and for a free max_in_flight slot.

Both are normally near zero. Limiter waits — a burst of cold keys or a restart; slot waits — a slow upstream holds the slots.

**What to do:**
1. Slots — "Slot saturation" and "Upstream attempt duration".
2. Limiter — compare the source rate with its quota; raise it with the replica count in mind.
spec.title: Upstream waits (rate limiter, slots)
